initiative.title: Bring tsx-data-flow into srcly
initiative.summary: Headline: tsx-data-flow's route -> terminal data-flow graph rendered in srcly's dependency viewer, with the compiler-backed analysis (type checking, symbol identity, field lineage, frontiers) kept intact. Findings, metrics, markers, reports follow as supporting evidence. srcly stays the fast base layer.
initiative.next_action: Pro threads refine branches; plan first proof: export one route's totality evidence into a data-flow contract and render in the current deps canvas.

sources.anchor: product priority order; code map primary surface
Views table; Explore it in the browser
Findings row; Metrics end-to-end; Code viewer; Graph views
route -> terminal graph is the real want, 2026-10-23

claims.statement: srcly is the home and base layer; tsx-data-flow features merge into it.
srcly's speed must be preserved; data flow never delays the base render.
Value order (revised): route -> terminal data-flow graph in the dependency viewer first; findings/metrics/markers/reports support it.
Analysis correctness (compiler-backed identity, strict tsconfig) outranks everything else in tsx-data-flow.
Markdown output exists for agent handoff: dense, grounded, concise next action.
tsx-data-flow's own overview/report pages are transitional and need not survive.
Several Pro threads will detail branches and update this map.
Single repository: engine moves into srcly (workspace/monorepo layout only if needed).
tsx-dataflow-serve UI goes away; focus on best versions of features in srcly.
Distribution delegated to agent: choose most robust. Chosen: esbuild bundle in the wheel, system node>=18, project typescript with bundled fallback, N/A without node.
The real want is the route -> terminal data viz (Route Totality) shown in srcly dependency viewer.
All tsx-data-flow type checking and analysis logic is to be maintained.
srcly has better visuals and selection and should own the graph experience.

themes: evidence from engine, picture from srcly

conflicts.statement: tsx-data-flow says the code map is its primary surface; srcly's primary surface is the map/treemap with a modal code viewer.
conflicts.resolution: srcly's treemap stays primary; the code viewer absorbs code-map overlays (path on source, markers, where-used).

shape.appetite: Program delivered as independently revertible slices, one srcly home per slice.
shape.problem: Two tools with overlapping shells; srcly is fast but tree-sitter-only, tsx-data-flow is deep but slow and has its own UI.
shape.recommended_shape: Engine supplies evidence, srcly supplies the picture: engine (in engine/, bundled in wheel) emits a data-flow graph in srcly contract style (route -> occurrence -> step hierarchy + typed proven edges); srcly's dependency view renders it in a Data flow mode with its canvas, focus, expand-in-place, hover, keyboard and code opening. Findings/metrics/markers/reports flow through existing srcly pipelines.

feature_mapping.tsx_feature: Route Totality / Data trajectories graph (route -> component occurrences -> field lineage -> terminals, frontiers)
feature_mapping.srcly_home: client/src/viz/deps Data flow mode + new data-flow graph contract

feature_mapping.tsx_feature: Route discovery, occurrence surface, field lineage/proof, value summaries, type checking (src/analysis)
Field reach / selected-path projections, isolation with boundary stubs
Render-path findings, defensive-ledger, impossible defenses, repeated forks, context relay
Burden, path depth, representation changes, defensive ops, prop relay, fan-out/in
Route Totality canvas/camera/layout/disclosure UI (~9.6K lines), component topology, world map
feature_mapping.srcly_home: replaced by srcly deps canvas; not migrated

feature_mapping.tsx_feature: tsx-dataflow-serve overview, file rows, report pages

success_moves: Emit data-flow evidence in srcly's graph-contract style (hierarchy + typed edges) so the existing canvas, roll-up, expand-in-place and keyboard work unchanged.
Prove on existing route-totality evidence with no new layout code before deciding on a route-specific layout rule.
Move the analysis intact into engine/; replace only the UI, never the evidence.
Keep the engine off the critical path: background program build, route inventory, per-route detail on demand, N/A with reasons.
Coordinate layout changes with dependency-graph-legibility (active in viz/deps/layout.ts).
Route all supporting signals through catalog metrics, findings and markers so treemap, Hot Spots, compare and report derive automatically.

first_proof.question: Can srcly's existing dependency canvas present one route's totality evidence as legibly as Route Totality, with field reach, one path, and code opening?
first_proof.artifact: Data-flow contract export for examples/solid-route then visual-notes /time-blocks, rendered in the current deps canvas with field selection and node -> code viewer.
first_proof.decision_rule: Packing reads well -> extend it; top-down flow fights it -> add one route layout rule inside the same canvas; missing ordered steps -> add the smallest analyzer fact, never an invented step.

rabbit_holes: Embedding tsx-data-flow's SPA or route-totality graph wholesale.
200K-LOC repos: engine takes ~120s; needs scoping (changed files, per-package) or a skip rule.
Monorepos with many tsconfigs: bound projects like MAX_TSC_PROJECTS.
Wheel size from bundled TypeScript fallback; measure in first proof.
Porting tsx-data-flow's graph layout/camera instead of using srcly's.
Fields with dozens of destinations rendered as a wall instead of grouped broad-use.

history.event: Initiative created; intent and shape drafted from the user's request plus both repos' docs.
Resolved D1 (single repo, engine/ package), D2 (bundle in wheel, delegated), D3 (retire serve UI). Shape updated; no downstream artifacts invalidated.
Intent revised: route -> terminal graph in dependency viewer is the headline; shape, mapping priorities and first proof regenerated.
